summary: Abigail I. MacBain works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at McMaster University (attested 2008), studying under Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, Mark MacWilliams, and Michael Greenwald.

Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron (1731–1805) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at the Sorbonne, Amersfoort, and under Darab Kumana, later holding posts at the Bibliothèque nationale and Institut de France.

Abraham Sachs (1914–1983) was a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1935–1939) and held appointments at the Institute for Advanced Study (1945) and Brown University (~1948–1983).
Abraham Zablocki specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Cornell University and held a position at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).
Acharya Buddharakkhita studied under U Nārada and Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1956). His students include Laurence Khantipalo Mills.

Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned an MA under David P. Jackson and a PhD (2005) under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg, later serving as a research associate at the University of Munich (2004–2006).

Adalbert Bezzenberger (1851–1922) worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and at Munich, he served as Privatdozent at Göttingen (1874) and professor of Sanskrit, prorector, and rector at Königsberg (1879–1921).

Adalbert Kuhn (1812–1881) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin (1833–1837) and served as teacher, professor, and director at Köllnisches Gymnasium between 1837 and 1870.

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his doctorate under Greg Bailey (attested 2004) and served as senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).

Adam Hardy (1953–) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1972–1976), he directed PRASADA (~1993) and became Professor of Asian Architecture at Cardiff University (~2005).

Adam Pearcey is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, while also studying under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers.

Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt (1955–) works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Erlangen-Nürnberg, Bonn, and Marburg, and held posts as guest professor at the University of Vienna (~2005) and Privatdozentin at Marburg (2009).

Adelheid Mette (1934–2023) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Hamburg, she served as professor of Middle Indic languages at the University of Munich (1980) and held the Indology chair at Münster (1988–2000).

Aden Kumler (1974–) is an art historian who studied at Chicago, Toronto, PIMS, and Harvard (Doktorat ~2001–2007). She taught at the University of Chicago (2007–2013) and became professor of older art history at Basel in 2020.
Adeu Rinpoche (1931–2007) was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Samten Gyatso and Drukpa Choegon Rinpoche, and he taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.
Adi Da (1939–2008) was active in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University (~1957–1961) and Stanford University (~1961–1963).

Adinath Neminath Upadhye (1906–1975) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and BORI. He lectured at Rajaram College (1930–1962), became Professor Emeritus at Shivaji University, and held the Jaina Chair at Mysore (1971).

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler (1807–1887) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bopp, Schlegel, and Lassen in Germany and Paris. From 1833 to 1872, he served as Professor of Sanskrit and librarian at the University of Breslau.

Adolf Holtzmann (1810–1870) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin, Munich, and Paris under Frank, Schmeller, and Burnouf, and served as professor of German literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University (1852–1870).

Adolf Kaegi (1849–1923) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Rudolf von Roth and Karl Friedrich Geldner at Zurich, Tübingen, and Leipzig, and held professorial chairs at the University of Zurich from 1883 to 1914.
